author: VANSMITHLAB
title: Why Fashion Stopped Trusting Photography
summary: Fashion film, platforms and AI video as a new dramaturgy of the fashion image

inline_media.after_heading: 1. Photography gave fashion the icon, but not its behaviour
inline_media.alt: Diagram of the transition from fashion photography through motion and editing to platform feeds and AI video.
inline_media.caption: One image now passes through four modes: photography, movement, sound with editing, and repetition in a feed or AI video.

inline_media.alt: Three lines compare the movement of silk, leather and knit over time.
inline_media.caption: Silk flows, leather resists and knit stretches: the surface of fabric becomes legible through duration.
inline_media.licence_or_permission: Original VANSMITHLAB editorial diagram; no third-party image copied.

inline_media.after_heading: 4. SHOWstudio: when process became part of the image
inline_media.alt: SHOWstudio diagram linking concept, light and pose, live process, archive and viewer.
inline_media.caption: SHOWstudio changed more than the publication format: the studio process became screen content in its own right.
inline_media.licence_or_permission: Original VANSMITHLAB editorial diagram; no third-party image copied.

inline_media.after_heading: 5. NOWNESS and the short cultural form
inline_media.alt: Diagram placing fashion film within an editorial environment of fashion, art, music, architecture, portraiture and travel.
inline_media.caption: Within the NOWNESS editorial environment, fashion works beside other cultural disciplines rather than as an isolated advertisement.
inline_media.licence_or_permission: Original VANSMITHLAB editorial diagram; no third-party image copied.

inline_media.after_heading: 6. Women’s Tales: the brand as a series, not a single campaign
inline_media.alt: A timeline of five films shows how a recurring series accumulates a brand's screen memory.
inline_media.caption: Women’s Tales turns a one-off campaign into an ongoing frame for different directorial voices and heroines.
inline_media.licence_or_permission: Original VANSMITHLAB editorial diagram; no third-party image copied.

inline_media.after_heading: 7. Prada and GucciFest: the object becomes scene and character
inline_media.alt: Comparison of Prada, where the object acts as a psychological agent, and GucciFest, where the collection becomes a serial world.
inline_media.caption: Two cinematic modes: an object intervenes in the psychology of a scene, or a collection spreads across a serial world.
inline_media.licence_or_permission: Original VANSMITHLAB editorial diagram; no third-party image copied.

inline_media.after_heading: 8. The vertical screen and the economy of the first seconds
inline_media.alt: Comparison between slow fashion myth-making and a short vertical fragment designed to stop a swipe.
inline_media.caption: The contemporary image lives between two speeds: the atmosphere of long form and the instant gesture of the first seconds.
inline_media.licence_or_permission: Original VANSMITHLAB editorial diagram; no third-party image copied.

inline_media.after_heading: 9. AI video: photography moves again, but not through the camera
inline_media.alt: AI image-to-video diagram: a source image and poses become body and fabric motion, alongside risks concerning consent, authorship, physics, rights and trust.
inline_media.caption: Synthesised movement is not evidence of real movement: direction shifts toward control of source, body, fabric, consent and rights.
inline_media.licence_or_permission: Original VANSMITHLAB editorial diagram; no third-party image copied.
